settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: No validation is expected in a low-level document factory; the security decision is normally delegated to ExternalResourceSecurity strategies enforced by BridgeContext/UserAgent, which were not reviewed.

The DATASET's DefaultExternalResourceSecurity/EmbededExternalResourceSecurity implementations (read) show that external-resource policy is handled elsewhere, suggesting the factory is not the intended enforcement point.
candidates.description: SAXSVGDocumentFactory.createDocument(String uri) builds a ParsedURL directly from the uri argument and immediately calls purl.openStream(...), then derives the system id and charset from the resulting connection. There is no scheme/host allow-listing at this layer. If an attacker can influence the URI string passed to createSVGDocument/createDocument (e.g. an SVG source location or a nested/external reference resolved through this factory), the factory will open a connection to that URL. This is the pattern that underlies SSRF-style issues in SVG loaders. The actual reachability and any upstream validation were not established from the reviewed spans; other classes (callers such as transcoders, browser/viewer components, and ParsedURL itself) were not read.
missing_evidence: The callers of createDocument/createSVGDocument and whether they enforce any URL policy.
ParsedURL.openStream behavior and whether it restricts protocols/hosts.
BridgeContext checkLoadExternalResource wiring and the default UserAgent in the affected entry points (transcoder vs. viewer).
preconditions: Attacker can influence the URI string passed to SAXSVGDocumentFactory.createDocument/createSVGDocument (document location or a resolved external reference).
The calling context does not independently restrict the URL/scheme/host before invoking the factory.
candidates.title: SAXSVGDocumentFactory.createDocument opens a stream on an unvalidated caller-supplied URI

counter_evidence: The null-check at line 88 combined with the data-protocol allowance suggests the author intended null handling; only the ordering is wrong for this path.
No caller in the reviewed spans was observed passing null, so practical reachability is unproven.
candidates.description: In the DefaultExternalResourceSecurity constructor, when docURL is non-null the code reads externalResourceURL.getHost() at line 83 unconditionally. The explicit `externalResourceURL == null` guard appears later, at line 88, inside the host-mismatch branch, after the dereference. If a caller passes a null external resource URL together with a non-null document URL, execution hits a NullPointerException at line 83 instead of returning a proper decision. The Javadoc for the parameter (lines 66-69) states the parameter may be null when the xlink:href attribute was empty, so a null argument is an anticipated input. Impact observed is a denial/exception on null input rather than an access-control bypass, but the ordering indicates the guard is misplaced and ineffective for the null case it names.
missing_evidence: Callers that construct DefaultExternalResourceSecurity and whether they can supply a null resource URL.
Whether an exception here is caught and treated as a denial by the surrounding resource-loading code.
preconditions: A caller invokes new DefaultExternalResourceSecurity(null, docURL) with docURL non-null, e.g. an element whose xlink:href is empty.
candidates.title: DefaultExternalResourceSecurity dereferences externalResourceURL before its null check
